analysis:
All three changed files are documentation only. No code, configuration, endpoints or controls changed.

1) docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md: the only change is at head line 187, the 'Retirement and identity' row of the bounded shorter complete-checkpoint fallback table. It adds that a cold result returns only after its attempt's host IO refund has completed. This is a clarifying statement about read-retry and refund ordering. It does not change the DBK3 encryption, HMAC lookup tags, 30-minute TTL, identity bindings or epoch rules that T-041 and SEC-035 rely on. It fits with the existing no-retry-on-AR-allocation-refusal text at lines 183 and 189-197. I could not verify the described behavior against the SSDCheckpointStageReservation/waitForRefund implementation, because that source was not supplied. This is a documentation claim only and affects no security conclusion.

2) docs/reports/2026-10-15-nemotron-super-image-ingress.md is a new measurement report. It covers image decoder parity, CPU time, peak memory and tower working memory. It is CPU-only, with no model run. Its Limitations section (head lines 105-112) discloses that JPEG decoding is not bit-exact versus Pillow, that results are for one machine and OS build, and that no end-to-end test was run. It states that media reservations now add a tower bound; the decoder and reservation code is not in this PR. It introduces no new attack surface.

3) docs/reports/README.md adds a single index link to the new report.

No threat-model assumptions are invalidated. The decoder workspace quote and media memory reservation are possible DoS-related controls (provider availability, T-010/T-016 class). That code is outside this PR, so the next pass need not examine them.
